questions.stem: How many times larger is the volume of the second shape compared to the first shape?

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 460 215" style="max-width: 440px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><g stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="45,105 70,80 115,80 90,105" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="90,105 115,80 115,125 90,150" fill="#cbd5e1"/><polygon points="45,105 90,105 90,150 45,150" fill="#f1f5f9"/><line x1="84" y1="127.5" x2="96" y2="127.5" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="98" y1="133" x2="107" y2="142" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="67.5" y1="145" x2="67.5" y2="165" stroke-width="1.5"/></g><text x="67.5" y="182" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#0f172a" text-anchor="middle">2cm</text><g stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="230,70 275,25 365,25 320,70" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="320,70 365,25 365,115 320,160" fill="#cbd5e1"/><polygon points="230,70 320,70 320,160 230,160" fill="#f1f5f9"/><line x1="313" y1="115" x2="327" y2="115" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="337" y1="132" x2="348" y2="143" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="275" y1="154" x2="275" y2="175" stroke-width="1.5"/></g><text x="275" y="192" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#0f172a" text-anchor="middle">4cm</text></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the volume of the first (smaller) cube
steps.work:
The smaller cube has a side length of \(s_1 = 2\text{ cm}\):

\[\text{Volume}_1 = s_1^3 = 2^3 = 8\text{ cm}^3\]

steps.explain: Calculate the volume of the second (larger) cube
steps.work:
The larger cube has a side length of \(s_2 = 4\text{ cm}\):

\[\text{Volume}_2 = s_2^3 = 4^3 = 64\text{ cm}^3\]

steps.explain: Compare their volumes
steps.work:
Divide the larger volume by the smaller volume:

\[\frac{\text{Volume}_2}{\text{Volume}_1} = \frac{64\text{ cm}^3}{8\text{ cm}^3} = \mathbf{8}\]

Linear scale factor rule: When the linear dimensions scale by \(k = \frac{4}{2} = 2\), volume scales by \(k^3 = 2^3 = \mathbf{8}\).

questions.stem: How big is the angle between NE and S, going anticlockwise from NE?

steps.explain: Understand the angle between adjacent compass directions
steps.work:
A full revolution is \(360^\circ\). An 8-point compass divides the circle into 8 equal sectors:

\[\text{Angle per sector} = \frac{360^\circ}{8} = 45^\circ\]

steps.explain: Count the sectors moving anticlockwise from NE to S
steps.work:
Moving anticlockwise (counter-clockwise) starting from North-East (NE):

  1. From NE to N: \(1\) sector (\(45^\circ\))
  2. From N to NW: \(1\) sector (\(45^\circ\))
  3. From NW to W: \(1\) sector (\(45^\circ\))
  4. From W to SW: \(1\) sector (\(45^\circ\))
  5. From SW to S: \(1\) sector (\(45^\circ\))

Total sectors traversed = \(5\) sectors.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 280 280" style="max-width: 270px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><circle cx="140" cy="140" r="110" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-width="1.2"><line x1="140" y1="30" x2="140" y2="250"/><line x1="30" y1="140" x2="250" y2="140"/><line x1="62" y1="62" x2="218" y2="218"/><line x1="62" y1="218" x2="218" y2="62"/></g><path d="M203,77 A90,90 0 1 0 140,230" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="4,3"/><polygon points="140,234 135,222 145,222" fill="#dc2626"/><circle cx="203" cy="77" r="5" fill="#2563eb"/><circle cx="140" cy="230" r="5" fill="#dc2626"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a" text-anchor="middle"><text x="140" y="22">N</text><text x="226" y="58">NE</text><text x="265" y="145">E</text><text x="226" y="232">SE</text><text x="140" y="268">S</text><text x="54" y="232">SW</text><text x="15" y="145">W</text><text x="54" y="58">NW</text></g><rect x="80" y="125" width="120" height="30" rx="6" fill="#fef2f2" stroke="#fca5a5" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="140" y="145" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#dc2626" text-anchor="middle">225° anticlockwise</text></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the total angle
steps.work:
Multiply the number of sectors by \(45^\circ\):

\[\text{Total Angle} = 5 \times 45^\circ = \mathbf{225^\circ}\]

(Alternative method: The clockwise angle from NE to S is \(45^\circ + 90^\circ = 135^\circ\). Therefore, the anticlockwise angle is \(360^\circ - 135^\circ = 225^\circ\).)

questions.stem: If a sink drains at \(600\text{ mL}\) per second, and each litre of water costs 16 cents, how much does the water cost that has gone down the drain in 2 hours assuming the tap has been running water the entire time?

steps.explain: Calculate the total draining time in seconds
steps.work:
Convert \(2\text{ hours}\) into seconds:

\[\text{Time} = 2\text{ hours} \times 60\text{ min/hour} \times 60\text{ s/min} = 7200\text{ seconds}\]

steps.explain: Calculate the total volume of water drained in litres
steps.work:
Multiply the flow rate by the time in seconds:

\[\text{Volume in mL} = 600\text{ mL/s} \times 7200\text{ s} = 4{,}320{,}000\text{ mL}\]

Convert millilitres to litres (\(1\text{ L} = 1000\text{ mL}\)):

\[\text{Volume in Litres} = \frac{4{,}320{,}000}{1000} = 4320\text{ L}\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 135" style="max-width: 400px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="380" height="115" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><rect x="20" y="25" width="105" height="50" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="72" y="45" text-anchor="middle" fill="#64748b">Time</text><text x="72" y="63" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">7200 s</text><text x="135" y="55" font-size="16" fill="#94a3b8">×</text><rect x="148" y="25" width="105" height="50" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="200" y="45" text-anchor="middle" fill="#64748b">Flow Rate</text><text x="200" y="63" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">0.6 L/s</text><text x="263" y="55" font-size="16" fill="#94a3b8">=</text><rect x="275" y="25" width="105" height="50" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="327" y="45" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1e40af">Total Volume</text><text x="327" y="63" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#1d4ed8">4320 L</text><rect x="20" y="85" width="360" height="30" rx="6" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="200" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#065f46">Cost = 4320 L × $0.16 = $691.20</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the cost in dollars
steps.work:
Multiply litres by \(16\text{ cents}\) per litre:

\[\text{Cost in cents} = 4320 \times 16 = 69{,}120\text{ cents}\]

Convert cents to dollars:

\[\text{Cost in dollars} = \frac{69{,}120}{100} = \mathbf{\$691.20}\]

questions.stem: Joseph takes 2 hours and 30 minutes to finish a test, while Amelia can complete the same test in 5 hours. How long does it take them if they worked together?

steps.explain: Calculate the individual rate of work per hour
steps.work:
Express Joseph's completion time in hours: \(2\text{ hr } 30\text{ min} = 2.5\text{ hours} = \frac{5}{2}\text{ hours}\).

Their work rates (fraction of the test completed per hour) are:

  • Joseph: \(\frac{1}{2.5} = \frac{2}{5}\text{ of the test per hour}\)
  • Amelia: \(\frac{1}{5}\text{ of the test per hour}\)

steps.explain: Combine their work rates together
steps.work:
Add their hourly work rates:

\[\text{Combined Rate} = \frac{2}{5} + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{3}{5}\text{ of the test per hour}\]

steps.explain: Calculate the total time required in minutes
steps.work:
To complete \(1\) full test working together:

\[\text{Time in hours} = \frac{1}{\frac{3}{5}} = \frac{5}{3}\text{ hours}\]

Convert hours to minutes:

\[\text{Time in minutes} = \frac{5}{3} \times 60\text{ minutes} = 5 \times 20 = \mathbf{100\text{ minutes}}\]

questions.stem:
The cost of a taxi fare depends on the time taken as well as the distance covered.

Using the information given, which of the following statements must be true?

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 200" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><defs><marker id="axis-arrow" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" refX="3" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M1,1 L5,3 L1,5 Z" fill="#1e293b"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.8"><line x1="75" y1="160" x2="340" y2="160" marker-end="url(#axis-arrow)"/><line x1="75" y1="160" x2="75" y2="20" marker-end="url(#axis-arrow)"/><line x1="135" y1="155" x2="135" y2="165"/><line x1="195" y1="155" x2="195" y2="165"/><line x1="255" y1="155" x2="255" y2="165"/></g><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#0f172a"><text x="135" y="182" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="195" y="182" text-anchor="middle">6</text><text x="255" y="182" text-anchor="middle">9</text><text x="320" y="182">(Time)</text><text x="40" y="85" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">Cost of<tspan x="40" dy="16">the fare</tspan></text></g><g fill="#0f172a"><circle cx="195" cy="45" r="4.5"/><text x="206" y="49" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="600">Rob</text><circle cx="275" cy="85" r="4.5"/><text x="286" y="89" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="600">Bob</text><circle cx="275" cy="125" r="4.5"/><text x="286" y="129" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="600">Nob</text></g></svg>

options: The distance of Nob's fare was longer than Bob's fare.
Bob's fare was longer than Nob's and Rob's.
The distance of Rob's fare was the longest.

steps.explain: Understand the two factors that determine taxi fare
steps.work:
The cost of a taxi fare increases with both time taken and distance covered:

\[\text{Cost} = f(\text{time}, \text{distance})\]

For a given time, a greater distance results in a higher fare. Likewise, for a given distance, more time spent results in a higher fare.

steps.explain: Compare Rob's trip with Bob's and Nob's trips
steps.work:
From the scatter plot:

  • Rob's time: \(6\) time units (the shortest duration among all three passengers).
  • Bob and Nob's time: Approximately \(9.5\) time units (much longer duration than Rob).
  • Rob's cost: The highest point on the vertical axis (most expensive fare).

steps.explain: Deduce which statement must be true
steps.work:
Although Rob was in the taxi for the least amount of time, his fare was the most expensive. The only way this is possible is if he covered a significantly greater distance than Bob and Nob.

Therefore, the distance of Rob's fare was the longest must be true.

questions.stem: To promote the launch of a new breakfast cereal, a company is offering a "buy five, get one free" deal. If each box of cereal costs \(\$2.60\), how much would twenty-four boxes of cereal cost?

steps.explain: Understand the deal bundle size
steps.work:
Under the "buy 5, get 1 free" deal, every group of \(6\) boxes consists of:

  • \(5\) boxes paid
  • \(1\) box free

steps.explain: Calculate the number of bundles needed for 24 boxes
steps.work:
Divide the total \(24\) boxes into groups of \(6\):

\[\text{Number of groups} = \frac{24}{6} = 4\text{ groups}\]

For \(4\) groups:

  • Paid boxes: \(4 \times 5 = 20\text{ boxes}\)
  • Free boxes: \(4 \times 1 = 4\text{ boxes}\)

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><rect x="25" y="22" width="330" height="35" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="44" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">Buy 5, Get 1 Free  →  1 Group = 6 Boxes (5 Paid + 1 Free)</text><text x="25" y="78" font-weight="600" fill="#334155">24 boxes ÷ 6 = 4 groups</text><text x="25" y="95" font-weight="600" fill="#334155">Paid boxes = 4 × 5 = 20 boxes (Free = 4 × 1 = 4 boxes)</text><rect x="25" y="105" width="330" height="24" rx="4" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#065f46">Total Cost = 20 × $2.60 = $52.00</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the total cost
steps.work:
Multiply the number of paid boxes by the price per box (\(\$2.60\)):

\[\text{Total Cost} = 20 \times \$2.60 = \mathbf{\$52.00}\]

questions.stem: Helen spent two thirds of her money on dog food and \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the remainder on a movie ticket. If she had \(\$9\) left, how much money did she start with?

steps.explain: Work backwards to find the remainder before the movie ticket
steps.work:
Helen spent \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the remainder on a movie ticket, leaving \(1 - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{1}{4}\) of the remainder.

Since this remaining \(\frac{1}{4}\) equals \(\$9\):

\[\text{Remainder before movie} = \$9 \times 4 = \$36\]

steps.explain: Relate this remainder to the starting total money
steps.work:
Helen previously spent \(\frac{2}{3}\) of her starting money on dog food, leaving \(1 - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\) of her starting money.

Therefore, \(\frac{1}{3}\) of her starting money is equal to \(\$36\).

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 155" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="135" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><rect x="25" y="25" width="215" height="36" fill="#fee2e2" stroke="#fca5a5" stroke-width="1.2" rx="4"/><text x="132" y="48" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" fill="#991b1b">Dog Food: 2/3 ($72)</text><rect x="245" y="25" width="110" height="36" fill="#e0e7ff" stroke="#a5b4fc" stroke-width="1.2" rx="4"/><text x="300" y="48" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" fill="#3730a3">Remainder: 1/3 ($36)</text><g transform="translate(245, 68)"><rect x="0" y="0" width="80" height="28" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#fcd34d" stroke-width="1" rx="3"/><text x="40" y="18" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#92400e">Movie: 3/4 ($27)</text><rect x="84" y="0" width="26" height="28" fill="#dcfce7" stroke="#86efac" stroke-width="1.2" rx="3"/><text x="97" y="18" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" font-size="11" fill="#166534">$9</text></g><rect x="25" y="105" width="330" height="26" rx="4" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#86efac" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="123" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#15803d">Starting Amount = $9 × 4 × 3 = $108</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the initial starting amount
steps.work:
Multiply by \(3\) to find the full initial amount:

\[\text{Starting Money} = 36 \times 3 = \mathbf{\$108}\]

Check: \(\$108 \times \frac{2}{3} = \$72\) (dog food), leaving \(\$36\). Then \(\$36 \times \frac{3}{4} = \$27\) (movie), leaving \(\$36 - \$27 = \$9\) \(\checkmark\)

questions.stem:
\[\frac{3}{7} \times 56 + \frac{1}{3} \times 36 + \frac{1}{\theta} \times 32 = 40\]

The value of \(\theta\) is

steps.explain: Evaluate the first two multiplication terms
Sum the known terms and simplify the equation
steps.work:
Add the two values:

\[24 + 12 = 36\]

Substitute back into the original equation:

\[36 + \frac{32}{\theta} = 40\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12.5"><rect x="25" y="22" width="95" height="36" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1"/><text x="72" y="45" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">3/7 × 56 = 24</text><text x="130" y="45" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">+</text><rect x="145" y="22" width="95" height="36" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1"/><text x="192" y="45" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">1/3 × 36 = 12</text><text x="250" y="45" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">=</text><rect x="265" y="22" width="90" height="36" rx="6" fill="#f1f5f9" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="310" y="45" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#334155">36</text><rect x="25" y="70" width="330" height="55" rx="6" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="190" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#065f46">36 + 32/θ = 40  →  32/θ = 4</text><text x="190" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" font-size="14" fill="#047857">θ = 32 / 4 = 8</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Solve for theta
steps.work:
Subtract \(36\) from both sides:

\[\frac{32}{\theta} = 40 - 36 = 4\]

Multiply by \(\theta\) and divide by \(4\):

\[\theta = \frac{32}{4} = \mathbf{8}\]

questions.stem: At a wedding reception, a quarter of the people drank only champagne, one-third drank only lemonade, 18 people drank neither and 7 drank both. How many people were at the party?

steps.explain: Express the total guests as the sum of four disjoint groups
steps.work:
Let \(N\) be the total number of people at the reception. All guests belong to one of four mutually exclusive groups:

  • Only champagne: \(\frac{1}{4}N\)
  • Only lemonade: \(\frac{1}{3}N\)
  • Both drinks: \(7\) people
  • Neither drink: \(18\) people

\[\frac{1}{4}N + \frac{1}{3}N + 7 + 18 = N\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 200" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="180" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="150" cy="95" r="65" fill="rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.12)" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="1.8"/><circle cx="230" cy="95" r="65" fill="rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.12)" stroke="#10b981" stroke-width="1.8"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700"><text x="115" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1d4ed8">Champagne only<tspan x="115" dy="16">1/4 N (15)</tspan></text><text x="190" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#7c3aed">Both<tspan x="190" dy="16">7</tspan></text><text x="265" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#047857">Lemonade only<tspan x="265" dy="16">1/3 N (20)</tspan></text><text x="40" y="35" fill="#64748b">Neither = 18</text></g><rect x="40" y="155" width="300" height="25" rx="5" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#86efac" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="172" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#15803d" text-anchor="middle">1/4 N + 1/3 N + 7 + 18 = N  →  N = 60</text></svg>

steps.explain: Combine the fractions and integer terms
steps.work:
Add the two fractions with a common denominator of \(12\):

\[\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3}{12} + \frac{4}{12} = \frac{7}{12}\]

Add the integer values:

\[7 + 18 = 25\]

This gives the equation:

\[\frac{7}{12}N + 25 = N\]

steps.explain: Solve for the total number of guests N
steps.work:
Subtract \(\frac{7}{12}N\) from both sides:

\[N - \frac{7}{12}N = 25 \implies \frac{5}{12}N = 25\]

Multiply by \(\frac{12}{5}\):

\[N = 25 \times \frac{12}{5} = 5 \times 12 = \mathbf{60}\]

There were 60 people at the party.

parts.stem: How many axes of symmetry are there in the shape?

steps.explain: Analyze the rotational and reflection symmetry of the colored pattern
steps.work:
The overall boundary forms an equilateral triangle. Inside:

  • All \(6\) upright triangles are colored solid black.
  • All \(3\) inverted (downward-pointing) triangles are colored grey.

Because the shading pattern is identical from the perspective of each of the \(3\) vertices (a \(120^\circ\) rotational symmetry), reflection across each angle bisector preserves the exact coloring.

steps.explain: Count the lines (axes) of symmetry
steps.work:
An equilateral triangle with 3-fold symmetric coloring has exactly \(3\) axes of symmetry, each passing through one vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side:

\[\text{Number of axes of symmetry} = \mathbf{3}\]

questions.stem: One plate at the gym weighs 45 pounds. If Dennis can bench press 500 pounds, how many plates is that?

steps.explain: Divide the total weight by the weight of a single plate
steps.work:
To find how many 45-pound plates are in 500 pounds, divide:

\[\frac{500}{45} = \frac{100}{9} = 11\frac{1}{9} \approx 11.11\]

steps.explain: Compare whole plate multiples with the target weight
steps.work:
Check the total weight around 11 plates:

  • \(11\text{ plates} = 11 \times 45 = 495\text{ pounds}\) (only \(5\text{ lbs}\) away from \(500\))
  • \(12\text{ plates} = 12 \times 45 = 540\text{ pounds}\) (\(40\text{ lbs}\) over \(500\))

steps.explain: Select the nearest number of plates
steps.work:
\(11\frac{1}{9}\) rounds to the nearest whole integer 11.

questions.stem: Paula's grandfather clock gains 1 minute and 20 seconds every 3 hours. If his clock is showing the correct time at 4:00am, what time will it show at 1:00pm?

steps.explain: Calculate the total time elapsed between 4:00am and 1:00pm
Determine the number of 3-hour intervals and total time gained
steps.work:
The clock gains 1 minute and 20 seconds every 3 hours. Divide 9 hours by 3 hours:

\[\text{Number of intervals} = \frac{9\text{ hours}}{3\text{ hours}} = 3\text{ intervals}\]

Multiply the gain per interval by 3:

\[\text{Total gain} = 3 \times (1\text{ min } 20\text{ s}) = 3\text{ min } + 60\text{ s} = 4\text{ minutes}\]

questions.stem:
I have:

i.  four angles of 90°
ii.  four axes of symmetry
iii.  two pairs of parallel sides
iv.  my diagonals intersect at right angles

What shape am I?

meta.source: Selective Trial Test · Mathematical Reasoning

steps.explain: Narrow down candidates using angle and symmetry properties
steps.work:
Clue (i): Four \(90^\circ\) angles means the shape must be either a rectangle or a square. (Eliminates trapezium, parallelogram, and rhombus).

Clue (ii): A standard non-square rectangle only has 2 axes of symmetry (horizontal and vertical). A square has 4 axes of symmetry (2 medians + 2 diagonals).

steps.explain: Confirm using parallel sides and diagonal properties
steps.work:
Clue (iii): A square has two pairs of parallel opposite sides.

Clue (iv): In a square, the diagonals are perpendicular bisectors of each other (intersecting at right angles).

questions.stem:
If a train goes back and forth on a 5 km train line at 60km an hour, assuming that it does not slow down at all when reaching the end of the line and going the other way, how many times would the train have passed its starting point* in 2 and a half hours?
*Starting point is in the middle of the train line.

steps.explain: Calculate the total distance traveled by the train
Determine the distance between successive passes through the starting point
steps.work:
The starting point is at the midpoint (\(2.5\text{ km}\)) of the \(5\text{ km}\) line:

  • To reach an end and return to the starting point: \(2.5\text{ km} + 2.5\text{ km} = 5\text{ km}\)
  • Every subsequent pass through the midpoint also requires traveling \(5\text{ km}\) (reaching the other end and returning).

Therefore, the train passes its starting point exactly once every 5 km of travel.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 145" style="max-width: 400px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="380" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><text x="25" y="32" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">Total Distance = 60 km/h × 2.5 h = 150 km</text><g transform="translate(25, 48)"><line x1="10" y1="20" x2="340" y2="20" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="10" cy="20" r="5" fill="#ef4444"/><text x="10" y="38" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#475569">0 km</text><circle cx="175" cy="20" r="6" fill="#2563eb"/><text x="175" y="38" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" font-size="11" fill="#1d4ed8">Start (2.5 km)</text><circle cx="340" cy="20" r="5" fill="#ef4444"/><text x="340" y="38" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#475569">5 km</text></g><rect x="25" y="95" width="350" height="28" rx="5" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="200" y="114" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#065f46">Train passes Start once every 5 km: 150 ÷ 5 = 30 times</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the total number of passes
steps.work:
Divide the total distance by 5 km:

\[\text{Number of passes} = \frac{150\text{ km}}{5\text{ km}} = \mathbf{30\text{ times}}\]

questions.stem: Dennis, Neil, and Andrew have a win from a sport\'s bet, totalling to \(\$1305.00\). If Dennis has three quarters of what Neil has, and Andrew has two thirds of what Neil has, how much did Dennis get?

steps.explain: Express Dennis and Andrew's amounts in terms of Neil's share
steps.work:
Let \(N\) be the amount Neil received. Then:

  • Dennis: \(D = \frac{3}{4}N\)
  • Andrew: \(A = \frac{2}{3}N\)

steps.explain: Set up the total sum equation and solve for Neil's share
steps.work:
Sum of all three shares equals \(\$1305\):

\[\frac{3}{4}N + N + \frac{2}{3}N = 1305\]

Find a common denominator of 12:

\[\left(\frac{9}{12} + \frac{12}{12} + \frac{8}{12}\right)N = 1305 \implies \frac{29}{12}N = 1305\]

\[N = 1305 \times \frac{12}{29} = 45 \times 12 = \$540\]

questions.stem:
Questions 7 and 8 use the following information.

The fifth number of a sequence is 26.8 and the thirteenth is 48.4.

parts.stem: What is the eleventh number of that sequence?

steps.explain: Find the common difference of the arithmetic sequence
steps.work:
The sequence progresses from the 5th number (\(26.8\)) to the 13th number (\(48.4\)) over \(13 - 5 = 8\) steps:

\[d = \frac{48.4 - 26.8}{8} = \frac{21.6}{8} = \mathbf{2.7}\]

steps.explain: Calculate the eleventh number
steps.work:
The 11th number is 2 steps before the 13th number:

\[T_{11} = 48.4 - 2 \times 2.7 = 48.4 - 5.4 = \mathbf{43.0}\]

(Or moving forward from the 5th number: \(26.8 + 6 \times 2.7 = 26.8 + 16.2 = 43.0\).)

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 135" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="115" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><text x="25" y="32" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">Common Difference: (48.4 − 26.8) ÷ 8 = 2.7</text><g transform="translate(25, 45)"><rect x="0" y="0" width="85" height="32" rx="4" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="42" y="20" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">T₅ = 26.8</text><text x="100" y="16" font-size="11" fill="#2563eb">+6×2.7 →</text><rect x="145" y="0" width="85" height="32" rx="4" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="187" y="20" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#1d4ed8">T₁₁ = 43.0</text><text x="245" y="16" font-size="11" fill="#2563eb">+2×2.7 →</text><rect x="290" y="0" width="60" height="32" rx="4" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="320" y="20" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">T₁₃ = 48.4</text></g><rect x="25" y="88" width="330" height="26" rx="4" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#065f46">T₁₁ = 48.4 − 2(2.7) = 43.0</text></g></svg>

parts.stem: Which is not a number in the sequence?

steps.explain: Understand the condition for a number to belong to the sequence
steps.work:
Any number \(x\) in the sequence must differ from a known term (such as \(26.8\)) by an integer multiple of the common difference \(d = 2.7\):

\[\frac{x - 26.8}{2.7} \in \mathbb{Z}\]

steps.explain: Test each candidate option
steps.work:
Test the options:

  • \(29.5 - 26.8 = 2.7 = 1 \times 2.7\) (6th term) \(\checkmark\)
  • \(24.1 - 26.8 = -2.7 = -1 \times 2.7\) (4th term) \(\checkmark\)
  • \(51.1 - 48.4 = 2.7 = 1 \times 2.7\) (14th term) \(\checkmark\)
  • \(53.8 - 48.4 = 5.4 = 2 \times 2.7\) (15th term) \(\checkmark\)
  • \(46.7 - 26.8 = 19.9 \implies \frac{19.9}{2.7} \approx 7.37\) (Not an integer!)

steps.explain: Conclude the number not in the sequence
steps.work: Therefore, 46.7 is not a number in the sequence.

steps.explain: Calculate the area of a single grid square
steps.work:
Each grid square has dimensions \(3\text{ cm} \times 3\text{ cm}\):

\[\text{Area of 1 square unit} = 3\text{ cm} \times 3\text{ cm} = 9\text{ cm}^2\]

steps.explain: Count the number of square units covered by the polygon
steps.work:
By decomposing the polygon into triangles and rectangles (or using Pick's theorem / coordinates):

  • Left section (columns 0–2): \(4.5\) square units
  • Center V-notch section (columns 2–5): \(6.5\) square units
  • Right wing section (columns 5–7): \(2.5\) square units
  • Lower large triangle (columns 3–7, rows 4–7): \(5\) square units

\[\text{Total square units} = 4.5 + 6.5 + 2.5 + 5 = 18.5\text{ units}^2\]

steps.explain: Convert square units to square centimetres
steps.work:
Multiply the number of grid squares by the area of one square:

\[\text{Total Area} = 18.5 \times 9\text{ cm}^2 = \mathbf{166.5\text{ cm}^2}\]

questions.stem: Philip's heart rate is 4320 beats per hour. What is his heart rate per second?

steps.explain: Convert 1 hour into total seconds
steps.work:
There are \(60\) minutes in an hour, and \(60\) seconds in a minute:

\[1\text{ hour} = 60 \times 60 = 3600\text{ seconds}\]

steps.explain: Calculate beats per second by division
steps.work:
Divide the total beats by the total number of seconds:

\[\text{Heart rate per second} = \frac{4320\text{ beats}}{3600\text{ seconds}} = \frac{432}{360}\]

Divide numerator and denominator by \(36\):

\[\frac{432 \div 36}{360 \div 36} = \frac{12}{10} = \mathbf{1.2\text{ beats per second}}\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 135" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="115" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><rect x="20" y="25" width="100" height="44" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="70" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="#64748b">Per Hour</text><text x="70" y="60" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">4320 beats</text><text x="130" y="50" font-size="13" fill="#64748b">÷60 →</text><rect x="150" y="25" width="100" height="44" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="200" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1e40af">Per Minute</text><text x="200" y="60" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#1d4ed8">72 beats</text><text x="260" y="50" font-size="13" fill="#64748b">÷60 →</text><rect x="280" y="25" width="80" height="44" rx="6" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="320" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="#065f46">Per Second</text><text x="320" y="60" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#047857">1.2 beats</text><rect x="20" y="82" width="340" height="30" rx="5" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#86efac" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="102" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#15803d">4320 ÷ 3600 = 1.2 beats per second</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Verify using a two-step unit conversion
steps.work:
Step 1 (Per minute): \[\frac{4320\text{ beats}}{60\text{ min}} = 72\text{ beats per minute}\]

Step 2 (Per second): \[\frac{72\text{ beats}}{60\text{ s}} = \mathbf{1.2\text{ beats per second}}\]

questions.stem: Samantha is ten years younger than her brother Michael. 40 times Samantha's age plus 20 times Michael's age is equal to 680. How old is Michael?

steps.explain: Express Michael and Samantha's ages algebraically
steps.work:
Let \(S\) be Samantha\'s age and \(M\) be Michael\'s age. Since Samantha is \(10\) years younger than Michael:

\[M = S + 10\]

steps.explain: Set up and solve the linear equation for Samantha's age

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><rect x="25" y="22" width="330" height="30" rx="5" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" fill="#1e40af">Michael is 10 years older: M = S + 10</text><text x="25" y="72" font-weight="600" fill="#334155">40S + 20(S + 10) = 680</text><text x="25" y="90" font-weight="600" fill="#334155">60S + 200 = 680  →  60S = 480  →  S = 8</text><rect x="25" y="102" width="330" height="24" rx="4" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="119" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#065f46">Michael's Age = S + 10 = 8 + 10 = 18</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Find Michael's age and verify
steps.work:
Substitute \(S = 8\) to find Michael\'s age:

\[M = 8 + 10 = \mathbf{18\text{ years old}}\]

Check: \(40(8) + 20(18) = 320 + 360 = 680\) \(\checkmark\)

questions.stem: On a deserted island, the temperature of the sand during the morning was 8.64°C, while the water surrounding the island was 2.87°C. By the afternoon, the water's temperature rose by 3.35°C while the sand temperature had fallen by a quarter. What was the difference in temperature?

steps.explain: Calculate the afternoon sand temperature
steps.work:
The morning sand temperature was \(8.64^\circ\text{C}\). Falling by a quarter (\(\frac{1}{4}\)) means \(\frac{3}{4}\) remains:

\[\text{Afternoon Sand} = 8.64 \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right) = 8.64 \times \frac{3}{4} = 6.48^\circ\text{C}\]

steps.explain: Calculate the afternoon water temperature
steps.work:
The morning water temperature was \(2.87^\circ\text{C}\). Add the \(3.35^\circ\text{C}\) rise:

\[\text{Afternoon Water} = 2.87 + 3.35 = 6.22^\circ\text{C}\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><rect x="25" y="22" width="155" height="52" rx="6" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#fcd34d" stroke-width="1"/><text x="102" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#92400e">Sand (Afternoon)</text><text x="102" y="55" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#78350f">Fell by 1/4: 8.64 × 3/4</text><text x="102" y="69" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#b45309">= 6.48°C</text><rect x="200" y="22" width="155" height="52" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1"/><text x="277" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">Water (Afternoon)</text><text x="277" y="55" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#1d4ed8">Rose by 3.35: 2.87 + 3.35</text><text x="277" y="69" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#1e40af">= 6.22°C</text><rect x="25" y="84" width="330" height="34" rx="6" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="190" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" font-size="13" fill="#065f46">Difference = 6.48°C − 6.22°C = 0.26°C</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Find the temperature difference
steps.work:
Subtract the water temperature from the sand temperature:

\[\text{Difference} = 6.48^\circ\text{C} - 6.22^\circ\text{C} = \mathbf{0.26^\circ\text{C}}\]

questions.stem: In October, 115 ml of water fell. In November, 121 ml of water fell and in December, 340 ml of water fell. What is the average approximate daily rainfall for these 3 months?

steps.explain: Calculate the total rainfall across the three months
steps.work:
Sum the rainfall amounts for October, November, and December:

\[\text{Total Rainfall} = 115 + 121 + 340 = 576\text{ ml}\]

steps.explain: Calculate the total number of days in the 3-month period
steps.work:
Count the days in each month:

  • October: \(31\text{ days}\)
  • November: \(30\text{ days}\)
  • December: \(31\text{ days}\)

\[\text{Total Days} = 31 + 30 + 31 = 92\text{ days}\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><rect x="25" y="22" width="100" height="44" rx="5" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="75" y="40" text-anchor="middle" fill="#64748b">October</text><text x="75" y="56" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">115 ml (31 d)</text><rect x="140" y="22" width="100" height="44" rx="5" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="40" text-anchor="middle" fill="#64748b">November</text><text x="190" y="56" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">121 ml (30 d)</text><rect x="255" y="22" width="100" height="44" rx="5" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="305" y="40" text-anchor="middle" fill="#64748b">December</text><text x="305" y="56" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">340 ml (31 d)</text><rect x="25" y="78" width="330" height="40" rx="6" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="190" y="96" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#065f46">Total Rainfall = 576 ml  |  Total Days = 92 days</text><text x="190" y="111" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#047857">Average = 576 ÷ 92 ≈ 6.26... ≈ 6.3 ml/day</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the average daily rainfall
steps.work:
Divide total rainfall by total days:

\[\text{Average Daily Rainfall} = \frac{576\text{ ml}}{92\text{ days}} = 6.2608...\text{ ml/day} \approx \mathbf{6.3\text{ ml}}\]

questions.stem:
In Dennis' room, there are 144 dolls and 60 doll houses.
What number should you divide each number by to find the ratio of dolls to doll houses most quickly?

steps.explain: Identify the mathematical property needed to simplify a ratio in one step
steps.work: To simplify a ratio to its lowest integer terms most quickly (in a single division step), both quantities must be divided by their Highest Common Factor (HCF / GCD).

steps.explain: Find the prime factorisation of 144 and 60

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><rect x="25" y="22" width="155" height="44" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="102" y="40" text-anchor="middle" fill="#64748b">Prime Factors of 144</text><text x="102" y="56" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">2⁴ × 3² = 12 × 12</text><rect x="200" y="22" width="155" height="44" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="277" y="40" text-anchor="middle" fill="#64748b">Prime Factors of 60</text><text x="277" y="56" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">2² × 3 × 5 = 12 × 5</text><rect x="25" y="78" width="330" height="40" rx="6" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="190" y="96" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#065f46">Highest Common Factor (HCF) = 12</text><text x="190" y="111" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#047857">144 ÷ 12 : 60 ÷ 12 = 12 : 5</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Compute the HCF and verify the simplified ratio
steps.work:
Take the lowest power of all common prime factors:

\[\text{HCF}(144, 60) = 2^2 \times 3^1 = 4 \times 3 = \mathbf{12}\]

Dividing both by 12 yields the ratio in simplest form:

\[\frac{144}{12} : \frac{60}{12} = 12 : 5\]

parts.stem: By how much was the average rainfall higher in Adelaide compared to Perth in November?

steps.explain: Read the November rainfall values from the chart
steps.work:
From the bar chart for November:

  • Adelaide (white bar) = \(40\text{ mm}\)
  • Perth (black bar) = \(20\text{ mm}\)

steps.explain: Calculate the difference in millimetres and convert to centimetres
steps.work:
Subtract Perth\'s rainfall from Adelaide\'s rainfall:

\[\text{Difference} = 40\text{ mm} - 20\text{ mm} = 20\text{ mm}\]

Convert millimetres to centimetres (\(1\text{ cm} = 10\text{ mm}\)):

\[20\text{ mm} = \frac{20}{10}\text{ cm} = \mathbf{2\text{ cm}}\]

parts.stem: What was the range in the average monthly rainfall for Adelaide?

steps.explain: Identify the maximum and minimum monthly rainfall for Adelaide
steps.work:
Looking at the Adelaide (white) bars across all 12 months:

  • Maximum: May = \(120\text{ mm}\)
  • Minimum: November & December = \(40\text{ mm}\)

steps.explain: Calculate the range and convert the unit
steps.work:
The range is the difference between maximum and minimum:

\[\text{Range} = 120\text{ mm} - 40\text{ mm} = 80\text{ mm}\]

Convert to centimetres (\(1\text{ cm} = 10\text{ mm}\)):

\[80\text{ mm} = \frac{80}{10}\text{ cm} = \mathbf{8\text{ cm}}\]

parts.stem:
What is the difference in the average monthly rainfall between Perth and Adelaide?
Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

steps.explain: Calculate the annual total rainfall for Adelaide and Perth
Find the difference and calculate the monthly average
steps.work:
Subtract the totals to find the annual difference:

\[\text{Annual Difference} = 830\text{ mm} - 510\text{ mm} = 320\text{ mm}\]

Divide by 12 months to get the average monthly difference:

\[\text{Average Monthly Difference} = \frac{320\text{ mm}}{12} \approx 26.67\text{ mm}\]

Rounding to the nearest whole number gives 27 mm.

steps.explain: Find the third angle inside the left right-angled triangle
steps.work:
In the left right-angled triangle, the sum of interior angles is \(180^\circ\):

\[90^\circ + 45^\circ + \theta = 180^\circ\]

\[\theta = 180^\circ - 135^\circ = 45^\circ\]

So the interior angle at the intersection point is \(45^\circ\).

steps.explain: Use the straight-line angle property to find angle Y
steps.work:
The horizontal line is a straight line, which forms an angle of \(180^\circ\). Angle \(Y\) and the interior angle \(45^\circ\) form a supplementary linear pair:

\[Y + 45^\circ = 180^\circ\]

\[Y = 180^\circ - 45^\circ = \mathbf{135^\circ}\]

(Note: The \(60^\circ\) angle in the right triangle is extra information and is not required to solve for \(Y\).)

steps.explain: Find the combined value of ● and △ using Row 3
steps.work:
Look at Row 3, which consists only of ● and △:

\[2 \times ● + 2 \times △ = 20 \implies ● + △ = 10\]

steps.explain: Find the values of □, ●, and △ using Column 1 and Row 2
Calculate the value of ★ using Row 1
steps.work:
Substitute the known values \(● = 4\) and \(△ = 6\) into Row 1:

\[● + △ + ★ + △ = 25\]

\[4 + 6 + ★ + 6 = 25\]

\[16 + ★ = 25 \implies ★ = 25 - 16 = \mathbf{9}\]

(Check with Column 3: \(9 + 2(8) + 6 = 9 + 16 + 6 = 31\), which matches.)

questions.stem: Calculate the surface area of a cube with sides measuring 11 cm.

steps.explain: Recall the surface area formula for a cube
steps.work:
A cube consists of 6 identical square faces. For a side length \(s = 11\text{ cm}\):

\[\text{Surface Area} = 6 \times s^2\]

steps.explain: Calculate the area of one face
steps.work:
Multiply side length by side length:

\[\text{Area of 1 face} = 11\text{ cm} \times 11\text{ cm} = 121\text{ cm}^2\]

steps.explain: Multiply by 6 faces to find total surface area
steps.work:
Multiply the single face area by 6:

\[\text{Total Surface Area} = 6 \times 121\text{ cm}^2 = \mathbf{726\text{ cm}^2}\]

steps.explain: Analyze painted faces of a single-layer cube structure
steps.work:
The 3D shape is 1 cube deep (consisting of \(13\) unit cubes in total). Because the entire outside is painted:

  • Every cube has its front face painted.
  • Every cube has its back face painted.

Therefore, every cube already has at least \(2\) painted faces.

steps.explain: Identify the condition for exactly three painted faces
steps.work:
For a cube to have only 3 painted faces, it must have exactly 1 additional face exposed (from top, bottom, left, or right).

This means the cube must touch other cubes on 3 of its 4 side edges, leaving exactly one outer edge exposed.

steps.explain: Count the qualifying cubes row by row
steps.work:
Checking each row:

  • Top row (4 cubes): The 2nd and 3rd cubes from the left are surrounded on the left, right, and bottom (only their top face is exposed) \( ightarrow\) 2 cubes.
  • Middle row (6 cubes): The 1st cube on the left is surrounded on top, right, and bottom (only left exposed). The 4th cube from the left is surrounded on top, left, and right (only bottom exposed) \( ightarrow\) 2 cubes.
  • Bottom row (3 cubes): The 2nd cube from the left is surrounded on the left, top, and right (only bottom exposed) \( ightarrow\) 1 cube.

\[ ext{Total} = 2 + 2 + 1 = \mathbf{5 ext{ cubes}}\]

steps.explain: Substitute the numerical values into the expression
steps.work:
Substitute the given value for each shape:

  • Hexagon (⬡) = \(6\)
  • Triangle (△) = \(2\)
  • Pentagon (⬠) = \(\frac{3}{4}\)
  • Square (□) = \(\frac{1}{2}\)

This gives the numerical expression:

\[6 \div 2 - \frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\]

steps.explain: Perform division first following the order of operations
steps.work:
Following BODMAS/PEMDAS, division has higher priority than addition and subtraction:

\[6 \div 2 = 3\]

Now the expression is:

\[3 - \frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\]

Division first: 6 ÷ 2 = 3</text><text x="25" y="74" fill="#334155">2. Substitute: 3 − 3/4 + 1/2</text><rect x="25" y="82" width="370" height="25" rx="4" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="210" y="99" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#065f46">3 − 3/4 + 2/4 = 3 − 1/4 = 2 3/4</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the fraction operations using common denominators
steps.work:
Express all terms with a common denominator of 4:

\[3 = \frac{12}{4}, \quad \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{4}\]

\[\frac{12}{4} - \frac{3}{4} + \frac{2}{4} = \frac{12 - 3 + 2}{4} = \frac{11}{4} = \mathbf{2\frac{3}{4}}\]

questions.stem: In a certain country there are 3 different cultures: Ooga, Booga, Wooga. There are 2000 Oogas, 8000 Boogas and 4000 Woogas. Half of the Oogas are woogas and 1000 of the Boogas are Woogas. However none of the Boogas are Oogas. How many Woogas exist such that they are only Wooga and not Booga or Ooga?

steps.explain: Find the number of Woogas who are also Oogas
steps.work:
We are told that half of the 2000 Oogas are Woogas:

\[\text{Ooga-Woogas} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2000 = 1000\]

steps.explain: Find the number of Woogas who are also Boogas
steps.work:
We are told that \(1000\) Boogas are Woogas:

\[\text{Booga-Woogas} = 1000\]

steps.explain: Use the disjoint culture condition to calculate "Only Wooga"
steps.work:
Since none of the Boogas are Oogas, the overlap between Boogas and Oogas is \(0\). Therefore, no one can belong to all three cultures.

Subtract both overlapping groups from the total Wooga population (\(4000\)):

\[\text{Only Wooga} = 4000 - 1000 (\text{Ooga}) - 1000 (\text{Booga}) = \mathbf{2000}\]

parts.stem: How many Year 6 students were surveyed altogether?

steps.explain: Calculate the combined percentage for Popcorn and Chocolate
steps.work:
First convert the angle for Popcorn to a percentage:

\[ ext{Popcorn} = rac{36^\circ}{360^\circ} imes 100\% = 10\%\]

Chocolate is given as \(28\%\). Combined:

\[ ext{Popcorn} + ext{Chocolate} = 10\% + 28\% = 38\%\]

steps.explain: Find the percentage represented by the remaining snack categories
steps.work:
The remaining categories are Soft Drink, Chips, and Lollies:

\[ ext{Percentage} = 100\% - 38\% = 62\%\]

steps.explain: Sum the known student counts and calculate total students
steps.work:
Sum the student numbers for Soft Drink, Chips, and Lollies:

\[10 + 40 + 74 = 124 ext{ students}\]

Since \(124 ext{ students}\) represents \(62\%\) of the total:

\[1\% = rac{124}{62} = 2 ext{ students}\]

\[ ext{Total students (100\%)} = 2 imes 100 = \mathbf{200 ext{ students}}\]

questions.stem: Albert purchased 4 juice boxes and 3 chip packets for \(\$25.40\). Dennis bought 4 chip packets and 3 juice boxes for one dollar more. What is the cost difference between a packet of chips and a juice box?

steps.explain: Set up equations for Albert's and Dennis's purchases
steps.work:
Let \(J\) be the price of a juice box and \(C\) be the price of a packet of chips.

  • Albert: \(4J + 3C = \$25.40\) --- (1)
  • Dennis: \(3J + 4C = \$26.40\) (\(\$1\) more) --- (2)

steps.explain: Subtract Equation (1) from Equation (2)
steps.work:
Subtract Albert\'s equation directly from Dennis\'s equation:

\[(3J + 4C) - (4J + 3C) = \$26.40 - \$25.40\]

\[(4C - 3C) + (3J - 4J) = \$1.00\]

\[C - J = \mathbf{\$1.00}\]

steps.explain: Conclude the cost difference

questions.stem:
The shapes in this sequence follow a rule.

What is the rule?

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 500 110" style="max-width: 480px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><g fill="#1e293b"><g transform="translate(50, 55)"><circle cx="0" cy="0" r="28" fill="none" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="7"/><path d="M12,12 Q28,28 34,36 Q22,30 8,18 Z" fill="#1e293b"/></g><g transform="translate(150, 55)"><g transform="rotate(45)"><circle cx="0" cy="0" r="28" fill="none" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="7"/><path d="M12,12 Q28,28 34,36 Q22,30 8,18 Z" fill="#1e293b"/></g></g><g transform="translate(250, 55)"><g transform="rotate(90)"><circle cx="0" cy="0" r="28" fill="none" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="7"/><path d="M12,12 Q28,28 34,36 Q22,30 8,18 Z" fill="#1e293b"/></g></g><g transform="translate(350, 55)"><g transform="rotate(135)"><circle cx="0" cy="0" r="28" fill="none" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="7"/><path d="M12,12 Q28,28 34,36 Q22,30 8,18 Z" fill="#1e293b"/></g></g><g transform="translate(450, 55)"><g transform="rotate(180)"><circle cx="0" cy="0" r="28" fill="none" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="7"/><path d="M12,12 Q28,28 34,36 Q22,30 8,18 Z" fill="#1e293b"/></g></g></g></svg>

steps.explain: Track the orientation of the tail of the shape
steps.work:
Look at the position of the tail on the letter-like shape in each consecutive step:

  1. 1st shape: Tail points down-right (South-East).
  2. 2nd shape: Tail points straight down (South).
  3. 3rd shape: Tail points down-left (South-West).
  4. 4th shape: Tail points straight left (West).
  5. 5th shape: Tail points up-left (North-West).

steps.explain: Calculate the degree and direction of rotation
steps.work:
From South-East to South is an angle of \(45^\circ\) in the clockwise direction. Each successive step turns exactly \(45^\circ\) clockwise:

\[\text{Rule} = \mathbf{\text{rotate } 45^\circ\text{ clockwise}}\]

questions.stem: Vivian has a 60 L bath which is filled to the brim. As the plug is stuck, she has to use a pump to pump out all the water. If the pump pumps water out at a rate of 1.5 L per minute, how long will it take for the pump to have pumped out 75% of the bath water?

steps.explain: Calculate the volume of water corresponding to 75% of the bath
steps.work:
Find 75% of the 60 L total bath capacity:

\[\text{Volume to pump} = 60\text{ L} \times 75\% = 60 \times \frac{3}{4} = 45\text{ litres}\]

steps.explain: Divide by the pump rate to find the total time in minutes
steps.work:
Divide the volume by the pumping rate of 1.5 L per minute:

\[\text{Time} = \frac{45\text{ L}}{1.5\text{ L/min}} = \frac{45}{\frac{3}{2}} = 45 \times \frac{2}{3} = \mathbf{30\text{ minutes}}\]

questions.stem: Riya did some vocabulary tests. Excluding the mark of her last exam, her average mark was 18. In her last test, she achieved a mark of 13, which brought her average down to 17. How many tests did Riya sit altogether?

steps.explain: Set up the algebraic equation for the total marks
steps.work:
Let \(n\) be the total number of tests Riya sat altogether (including the last exam). Then the number of tests before the last exam was \(n - 1\).

  • Total marks before last test: \(18 \times (n - 1)\)
  • Total marks after last test: \(17 \times n\)

steps.explain: Form and solve the equation with the last test score of 13
steps.work:
Adding the last test score (\(13\)) to the previous total gives the new total:

\[18(n - 1) + 13 = 17n\]

\[18n - 18 + 13 = 17n\]

\[18n - 5 = 17n \implies 18n - 17n = 5 \implies \mathbf{n = 5}\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><text x="25" y="32" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">Average Balance Equation:</text><text x="25" y="52" fill="#334155">Total before: 18 × (n − 1)</text><text x="25" y="70" fill="#334155">Total after adding 13: 18(n − 1) + 13 = 17n</text><text x="25" y="88" fill="#334155">18n − 5 = 17n  →  n = 5</text><rect x="25" y="96" width="330" height="26" rx="4" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="114" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#065f46">Total tests sat = 5 (Check: 4×18 + 13 = 85; 85÷5 = 17)</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Verify the solution
steps.work:
Check:

  • First 4 tests: \(4 \times 18 = 72\) total marks
  • 5th test: \(13\) marks \(\implies\) total = \(72 + 13 = 85\)
  • New average: \(\frac{85}{5} = 17\) \(\checkmark\)

Riya sat 5 tests altogether.

questions.stem: A certain garden has a path built around it. How long is the path? (Note: they are both parallelograms)

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 185" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><g stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="1.8" fill="none" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="40,140 210,140 230,50 60,50"/><polygon points="210,140 310,140 324.3,75.7 224.3,75.7"/></g><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13.5" font-weight="600" fill="#0f172a"><text x="125" y="162" text-anchor="middle">17 cm</text><text x="260" y="162" text-anchor="middle">10 cm</text><text x="198" y="98" text-anchor="end">7 cm</text><text x="332" y="112" text-anchor="start">5 cm</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Calculate the total length of the horizontal edges
steps.work:
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal:

  • Bottom path: \(17\text{ cm} + 10\text{ cm} = 27\text{ cm}\)
  • Top path: \(17\text{ cm} + 10\text{ cm} = 27\text{ cm}\)

\[\text{Horizontal Length} = 27\text{ cm} + 27\text{ cm} = 54\text{ cm}\]

steps.explain: Calculate the total length of the slanted outer edges
steps.work:
For the slanted sides:

  • Left outer slanted side: \(7\text{ cm}\)
  • Right outer slanted side: \(5\text{ cm}\)
  • Step where the large parallelogram extends above the small one: \(7\text{ cm} - 5\text{ cm} = 2\text{ cm}\)

\[\text{Slanted Length} = 7\text{ cm} + 5\text{ cm} + 2\text{ cm} = 14\text{ cm}\]

steps.explain: Sum all outer edges to find the total perimeter of the path
steps.work:
Add the horizontal and slanted components together:

\[\text{Total Path Length} = 54\text{ cm} + 14\text{ cm} = \mathbf{68\text{ cm}}\]

(Equivalent formula: \(2 \times (17 + 10) + 2 \times 7 = 54 + 14 = 68\text{ cm}\))

questions.stem: A reservoir is \(\frac{3}{7}\) full. If 120 litres of water is added, the reservoir is \(\frac{9}{11}\) full. What is the capacity (in litres) of the reservoir when full?

steps.explain: Calculate the fraction represented by the added 120 litres
steps.work:
Subtract the initial fraction from the final fraction with a common denominator of 77:

\[\Delta f = \frac{9}{11} - \frac{3}{7} = \frac{63 - 33}{77} = \frac{30}{77}\]

steps.explain: Relate this fraction to the added water volume
steps.work:
The \(\frac{30}{77}\) fraction of the reservoir corresponds to 120 litres:

\[\frac{30}{77} \times \text{Capacity} = 120\text{ L}\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><text x="25" y="32" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">Fraction Difference: 9/11 − 3/7 = 30/77</text><rect x="25" y="44" width="330" height="34" rx="5" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="65" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">30/77 of Capacity = 120 Litres</text><rect x="25" y="88" width="330" height="34" rx="5" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="190" y="103" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#065f46">1/77 of Capacity = 120 ÷ 30 = 4 L</text><text x="190" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#047857">Full Capacity (77/77) = 4 × 77 = 308 Litres</text></g></svg>

steps.explain: Solve for the full capacity
steps.work:
Find \(\frac{1}{77}\) of the capacity:

\[120 \div 30 = 4\text{ L}\]

Multiply by 77 for full capacity:

\[\text{Total Capacity} = 4 \times 77 = \mathbf{308\text{ litres}}\]

questions.stem:
Questions 34 and 35 use the following information.

In a lawn bowls club, there are 280 members, five sevenths of whom are men. All of the members participate in either bowling or scoring. Two fifths of the women and one half of men do bowling.

parts.stem: How many men do scoring?

steps.explain: Calculate the total number of men in the club
steps.work:
Five sevenths (\(\frac{5}{7}\)) of the 280 members are men:

\[\text{Number of men} = 280 \times \frac{5}{7} = 40 \times 5 = 200\text{ men}\]

steps.explain: Calculate how many men do scoring
steps.work:
One half (\(\frac{1}{2}\)) of the men do bowling, which means the other half do scoring:

\[\text{Men doing scoring} = 200 \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) = 200 \times \frac{1}{2} = \mathbf{100\text{ men}}\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 135" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="115" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><text x="25" y="32" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">Total Men = 280 × 5/7 = 200</text><g transform="translate(25, 45)"><rect x="0" y="0" width="160" height="34" rx="5" fill="#f1f5f9" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="80" y="18" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#475569">Men Bowling (1/2)</text><text x="80" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#334155">100</text><rect x="170" y="0" width="160" height="34" rx="5" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="250" y="18" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#1e40af">Men Scoring (1/2)</text><text x="250" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#1d4ed8">100</text></g><rect x="25" y="90" width="330" height="24" rx="4" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="190" y="107" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#065f46">Men who score = 200 ÷ 2 = 100</text></g></svg>

parts.stem: What fraction of all the members do scoring?

steps.explain: Calculate the number of women who do scoring
steps.work:
Total women in the club: \(280 - 200 = 80\text{ women}\).

Since \(\frac{2}{5}\) of women do bowling, \(\frac{3}{5}\) of women do scoring:

\[\text{Women doing scoring} = 80 \times \frac{3}{5} = 16 \times 3 = 48\text{ women}\]

steps.explain: Find total scoring members and express as a simplified fraction
steps.work:
Add scoring men and scoring women:

\[\text{Total scoring} = 100\text{ (men)} + 48\text{ (women)} = 148\text{ members}\]

Divide by the total club membership (280) and simplify by dividing by 4:

\[\text{Fraction} = \frac{148}{280} = \frac{148 \div 4}{280 \div 4} = \mathbf{\frac{37}{70}}\]

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 380 145" style="max-width: 380px; width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto;"><rect x="10" y="10" width="360" height="125" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12"><text x="25" y="30" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">Total Scorers:</text><text x="25" y="50" fill="#334155">• Men scoring: 100</text><text x="25" y="68" fill="#334155">• Women scoring: 80 × 3/5 = 48</text><text x="25" y="86" font-weight="600" fill="#334155">Total Scorers = 100 + 48 = 148</text><rect x="25" y="96" width="330" height="28" rx="5" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#a7f3d0" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="190" y="115" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="800" fill="#065f46">Fraction = 148 / 280 = 37 / 70</text></g></svg>

questions.stem: If 10 millimetres equal 1 centimetre, how many square centimetres does 1 square millimetre equal?
questions.hint: Area is length \(\times\) width, so the conversion factor must be used twice. Picture a square that is 1 cm by 1 cm and cut it into 1 mm by 1 mm squares.

keyPoints.note: The answer must be in cm² (an area unit), so convert using the length factor twice, not once.
A square millimetre is a square with sides of 1 mm, so each side is 0.1 cm.

steps.explain: Start with the given length conversion. 10 millimetres make 1 centimetre, so 1 cm is 10 times as long as 1 mm.
An area unit needs two lengths (length \(\times\) width). A square 1 cm by 1 cm is therefore 10 mm by 10 mm, so we must multiply 10 by itself.

questions.stem: If John gives Allen 5 dollars and Allen gives Frank 2 dollars, the three boys will have the same amount of money. If Frank had \(\$8\) originally, how much more money does John have than Allen?
questions.hint: Work backwards from the end. Frank started with \(\$8\) and only received money, so you can find what everyone ends with. Then undo each gift for John and Allen.

keyPoints.note: All three boys end with equal amounts. Frank's final amount tells you that common value.

keyPoints.text: how much more money does John have than Allen
keyPoints.note: You need the two STARTING amounts, then subtract: John − Allen.

steps.explain: Frank only receives \(\$2\) from Allen, so find Frank's amount at the end.
The three boys finish with the same amount, so John and Allen also end with \(\$10\) each.

steps.explain: Undo John's gift. John gave away \(\$5\) to end with \(\$10\), so he started with \(\$5\) more.

Undo Allen's two transactions. Allen received \(\$5\) from John (his money went up) and gave \(\$2\) to Frank (his money went down), so the net change is \(+\$3\). He ends with \(\$10\), so he started with \(\$3\) less.
steps.work: \(\text{Allen at the start}+5-2=10\Rightarrow\text{Allen at the start}=\$7\)

questions.stem: What is numeral value of 57 tens, 2 ones, 3 tenths, 6 hundredths and 5 thousandths?
questions.hint: Turn each part into a number first (57 tens is not 57!). Then add the parts, keeping each digit in its own place-value column.

keyPoints.note: 57 tens means 57 × 10 = 570, not 57.
The place values after the decimal point are tenths, hundredths, thousandths in that order.

steps.explain: Convert each part to its value. 57 tens means 57 groups of ten.
The ones, tenths, hundredths and thousandths are single digits placed in their columns.
Add the whole-number parts first.
Add the decimal parts: 0.3 + 0.06 = 0.36, then 0.36 + 0.005 = 0.365.
Put the whole and decimal parts together.

Check the digits in a place-value chart: 5 hundreds, 7 tens, 2 ones . 3 tenths, 6 hundredths, 5 thousandths. Options with the decimal point in the wrong place (5723.65, 57236.5) change the size of the number by 10 or 100 times.

questions.stem: Of the following units which would be more likely used to measure the amount of water in a bathtub?
questions.hint: Water in a bathtub is a volume (capacity) of liquid. Decide which unit has a sensible size: a bathtub holds about 150 to 200 of the right unit.

keyPoints.note: The amount of liquid is its capacity or volume, so look for a capacity unit (litres or millilitres), not a mass unit.
A bathtub is big, so choose the larger capacity unit.

steps.explain: Decide what is being measured. The amount of water in a bath is how much space the water takes up, which is its capacity (volume).
Kilograms and centigrams measure mass (weight), not capacity, so these two units are not suitable.
Litres and millilitres both measure capacity. Compare their sizes: 1 litre is 1000 millilitres.
A bathtub holds roughly 150 litres. In millilitres this would be a huge number, 150 000 mL, which is awkward. A small unit is used for small amounts (a spoon of medicine is about 5 mL).
So the sensible unit for a large amount of water like a bathtub is litres.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the five consecutive even numbers whose average is 12?
questions.hint: The average is the total shared out equally. If you know the average and how many numbers there are, you can undo the sharing.

keyPoints.note: average = sum ÷ number of values, so sum = average × number of values.
There are 5 numbers in the list — that is the number you multiply by.

steps.explain: Recall the meaning of an average (mean): add all the numbers, then divide by how many numbers there are.
Rearrange the formula to find the sum: multiply both sides by the number of values.
Substitute: the average is 12 and there are 5 numbers.
Multiply.
Check by finding the numbers. The middle number of 5 consecutive even numbers equals the average, 12, so they are 8, 10, 12, 14, 16.

questions.stem: Which of the following fractions is the equivalent of \(0.5\%\)?
questions.hint: Percent means “out of 100”. Write \(0.5\%\) as \(\dfrac{0.5}{100}\), then remove the decimal from the top by multiplying top and bottom by 10.

keyPoints.note: 0.5% is HALF of one percent, so it is smaller than 1% = 1/100.

steps.explain: Percent means “out of 100”, so write the percentage over 100.
The numerator is a decimal. Multiply the top and the bottom by 10 to make it a whole number (the fraction keeps the same value).
Simplify \(\dfrac{5}{1000}\) by dividing the top and bottom by their common factor 5.
Check with a decimal: \(0.5\%=0.005\) and \(\dfrac{1}{200}=1\div200=0.005\). \(\checkmark\) The fraction \(\dfrac{1}{20}\) equals \(5\%\) and \(\dfrac{1}{2000}\) equals \(0.05\%\), so they are wrong.

questions.stem: The weights of two ships are in the ratio of 5: 9. If together they weigh 5,600 tonnes, how many more tonnes does the larger ship weigh?
questions.hint: Add the ratio numbers to find the total number of parts, find the weight of one part, then multiply by the DIFFERENCE of the ratio numbers.

keyPoints.note: Ratio 5 : 9 means the first ship has 5 equal parts and the second has 9 equal parts.
You want the difference between the two weights, not the weight of the larger ship.

steps.explain: Find the total number of equal parts by adding the ratio numbers.

questions.stem: A class of 40 students is to be divided into smaller groups. If each group is to contain 3, 4, or 5 people, what is the largest number of groups possible?
questions.hint: To get the MOST groups, make the groups as small as possible. Use groups of 3 as much as you can, then deal with the students left over.

keyPoints.note: More groups means smaller groups, so start with the smallest allowed size, 3.
Every group must have exactly 3, 4 or 5 people, and nobody can be left out.

steps.explain: To make as many groups as possible, each group should be as small as possible. The smallest allowed group size is 3.
See how many groups of 3 fit into 40 students.
With 13 groups of 3 there is 1 student left over, who cannot form a group alone. Instead, take away one group of 3 (12 groups of 3 use 36 students) so that 4 students are left.
The 4 students left form one group of 4, which is allowed. Count the groups.
Check that 14 groups is impossible: even if every group were the smallest size 3, 14 groups would need 42 students, but there are only 40. \(\checkmark\)

questions.stem: If a train travels \(n\) kilometres in 5 hours, how many kilometres will it travel in 25 hours?
questions.hint: Compare the two times first: how many times longer is 25 hours than 5 hours? The distance grows by the same factor.

keyPoints.note: Find how many 5-hour blocks fit into 25 hours — the train repeats the same distance each block.
The letter n is just a number of kilometres; keep it as n in the answer.

steps.explain: The train covers \(n\) km every 5 hours. We need to know how many 5-hour blocks fit into 25 hours.
At the same speed each block gives \(n\) km, so 5 blocks give 5 times as far.
Check with the speed method: speed \(=\dfrac{n}{5}\) km/h, so in 25 hours the train travels speed \(\times\) time.

Test with a number: if \(n=10\) km in 5 hours (2 km/h), then in 25 hours it travels \(2\times25=50\) km, which equals \(5\times10\). \(\checkmark\) The answer \(25\times n\) would give 250 km, which is far too big.

questions.stem: Steven travels from Shanghai to Beijing by his car in 2 hours. If he reduces the speed of his car by 30km/hr, then he takes 3.2 hours for the same distance. Find the distance between the two towns.
questions.hint: The distance is the same on both trips. Let the usual speed be \(v\) km/h and write distance \(=\) speed \(\times\) time for each trip, then set them equal.

keyPoints.text: reduces the speed of his car by 30km/hr
keyPoints.note: The slower speed is (v − 30) km/h, where v is the original speed.
Both trips cover the same distance, so speed × time is equal for both.

steps.explain: Let the original speed be \(v\) km/h. The first trip takes 2 hours, so the distance is speed \(\times\) time.
On the second trip the speed is 30 km/h lower, \(v-30\), and the time is 3.2 hours.
The distance is the same, so the two expressions are equal.
Expand the bracket: multiply 3.2 by both \(v\) and 30.
Collect the \(v\) terms on one side: subtract \(2v\) from both sides, then add 96.
Now find the distance using the first trip.
Check with the second trip: speed \(80-30=50\) km/h for 3.2 hours. \(\checkmark\)

Triangle area = ½ × base × height, so base × height must equal 2 × 40 = 80.

Multiply both sides by 2 to remove the half. So the product \(x\times y\) must equal 80 for a possible triangle.

In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal: left \(=\) right and bottom \(=\) top. So the outer edges of P1 and P2 have the same total length.

So P1 and P2 have the same perimeter. We cannot say anything sure about their areas because the zigzag line does not split the parallelogram into two obviously equal halves, so the statements about area and the two “different perimeter” statements are not true.

questions.stem: Michelle wants to expand her flowerbed by increasing the length and width each by 2 metres. What will the new area of the flowerbed be, if L and W represent the original dimensions of the flowerbed's length and width?
questions.hint: First write the new length and the new width as expressions. Then use area \(=\) length \(\times\) width with the NEW sides.

keyPoints.text: increasing the length and width each by 2 metres
keyPoints.note: 'Increase by 2' means ADD 2 metres to each side (L + 2 and W + 2), not multiply by 2.
Area of a rectangle = length × width, using the new length and the new width.

steps.explain: The original flowerbed has length \(L\) and width \(W\).
Each side is increased by 2 metres, so we add 2 to each (we do not multiply).
The area of a rectangle is length times width. Use the new length and the new width, and put each in brackets so the 2 is added before multiplying.
Test with numbers: if \(L=5\) m and \(W=3\) m, the new flowerbed is 7 m by 5 m. Its area is 35 m\(^2\). Option D gives \((5+2)\times(3+2)=7\times5=35\). \(\checkmark\)
Option A gives \(2\times5\times3=30\), option B gives \(2\times8=16\), option C gives \(10+6=16\). None of these equals 35, so only D is correct.

questions.stem: What is the mathematical average of the number of days in a typical year, the number of days in a week, and the number of hours in a day?
questions.hint: First write down the three numbers (a typical year has 365 days). The average is their total divided by how many numbers there are.

keyPoints.note: A typical year is not a leap year, so it has 365 days.
Average = total of the numbers ÷ how many numbers. There are three numbers here, so divide by 3.

steps.explain: Write down each of the three numbers the question describes.
steps.work: \(\text{days in a typical year}=365,\quad\text{days in a week}=7,\quad\text{hours in a day}=24\)

steps.explain: The mathematical average (mean) is the sum of the numbers divided by how many numbers there are.
Add the three numbers: 365 + 7 = 372, then 372 + 24 = 396.
There are 3 numbers, so divide the sum by 3.
Check by multiplying back: the average times 3 must give the sum.

questions.stem: \(85\%\) of what number is 136?
questions.hint: 136 is 85 hundredths of the unknown number. Find what 1% is by dividing 136 by 85, then find 100%.

keyPoints.note: The unknown number is the WHOLE (100%). 136 is only a part of it, so the answer must be bigger than 136.

steps.explain: Call the unknown number \(N\). \(85\%\) of \(N\) equals 136. Write 85% as the decimal 0.85.
To find \(N\), undo the multiplication by dividing both sides by 0.85.
Easier way: first find 1%. Since 85% is 136, divide by 85.
Then 100% is 100 times 1%.
Check: 85% of 160 should be 136. Since 10% of 160 is 16, 80% is 128 and 5% is 8, so 85% is 128 + 8.

questions.stem: The Chinese Calendar is based on a twelve-year cycle. Each year in the cycle corresponds to an animal: tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, sheep (or goat), monkey, rooster, dog, pig, rat and ox. The order of the animals never changes. The year 2010 in the Chinese Calendar is the Year of the Tiger. Which animal will mark the year 2111?
questions.hint: The animals repeat every 12 years. Find how many years pass from 2010 to 2111, then divide by 12 and look at the remainder to see how far to move along the list from the tiger.

keyPoints.note: After every 12 years the animals start again, so only the remainder when dividing by 12 matters.
Count the number of years from 2010 to 2111: subtract the two years.

steps.explain: Find how many years pass from the Year of the Tiger (2010) to 2111.
The cycle repeats every 12 years. Divide 101 by 12 to see how many full cycles there are and what is left over.
8 full cycles bring us back to the tiger. The remainder 5 tells us to move 5 animals forward from the tiger.
Count along the list: 1 rabbit, 2 dragon, 3 snake, 4 horse, 5 sheep.
Check: 2010 + 96 = 2106 is a tiger year (96 is a multiple of 12). Then 2107 rabbit, 2108 dragon, 2109 snake, 2110 horse, 2111 sheep. \(\checkmark\)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a true statement?
options: The product of two negative numbers is negative.
The product of one negative and one positive is positive.
When dividing a positive number by a negative number, the results are negative.
When dividing a negative number by a positive number, the results are positive.
questions.hint: Test each statement with small numbers such as 6 and 3 (and their negatives). Remember: two numbers with the SAME sign give a positive result; DIFFERENT signs give a negative result.

keyPoints.note: Only one statement is true. Test each with an example; one counter-example makes a statement false.

steps.explain: Recall the sign rules for multiplying and dividing: same signs give a positive answer, different signs give a negative answer.
Statement A says the product of two negatives is negative. Test with \(-2\) and \(-3\).
Statement B says negative times positive is positive. Test with \(-2\) and \(3\).
Statement C says a positive divided by a negative is negative. Test with 6 and \(-3\). This one is true.
Statement D says a negative divided by a positive is positive. Test with \(-6\) and 3.
A, B and D are false (each answer has the wrong sign) and only C is true.

questions.stem: A men's basketball team won 24 games and lost 32. What is the ratio of games lost to the number of games played?
questions.hint: The ratio is “lost : played” in that order. Played is NOT the same as won, so first find the total number of games played.

keyPoints.text: lost to the number of games played
keyPoints.note: The second number in the ratio is the TOTAL games played (won + lost), not the games won.
Won 24 and lost 32. Played = 24 + 32.

steps.explain: Find the total number of games played: the games won plus the games lost.
Write the ratio in the order asked: games lost first, then games played.
Simplify by dividing both numbers by their highest common factor, 8.
The simplified ratio is 4 : 7.

Check the other options: \(32:24\) is lost : won, \(3:4\) is won : lost, and \(4:2\) is not even a ratio of these numbers. Also \(4:7\) means 4 lost out of every 7 games played, and \(\dfrac{32}{56}=\dfrac47\). \(\checkmark\)

questions.stem: In a certain baseball league, each team plays 160 games. After playing half of their games, team A has won 60 games and team B has won 49 games. If team A wins half of its remaining games, how many more games must team B win to have the same record as team A at the end of the season?
questions.hint: Find how many games are left, then work out team A's total wins at the end of the season. Team B has to reach that same total.

keyPoints.note: Half of 160 games have been played, so half (80 games) remain.

keyPoints.text: how many more games must team B win
keyPoints.note: Final answer = A's total wins − the 49 wins B already has.

steps.explain: Half of the 160 games have been played. So 80 games are played and 80 games remain.
Team A wins half of its remaining games.
Add this to the 60 games A has already won to find A's wins for the whole season.
Team B needs the same record, 100 wins, but has won 49 so far. Subtract to find how many more wins B needs.
Check: B has 80 games left and needs 51 wins, which is possible. \(49+51=100\) wins, the same as team A. \(\checkmark\)

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two lengths of 6 cm and 9 cm. An equilateral triangle has the same perimeter. What is the length in centimetres of each side of the equilateral triangle?
questions.hint: Read the first sentence as: two sides are 6 cm and the third side is 9 cm. Add the three sides to get the perimeter, then share it equally between the 3 sides of the equilateral triangle.

keyPoints.text: two lengths of 6 cm and 9 cm
keyPoints.note: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides: two sides of 6 cm, and the third side is 9 cm.
Perimeter = sum of all three sides. An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides, so each side = perimeter ÷ 3.

steps.explain: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides. Here the two equal sides are 6 cm each and the third side is 9 cm (orange and blue in the diagram).
